requirements.requirement: node1 provides an NFSv4 export of /srv/nfs/shared to node2 and node3 over the dedicated storage network.
requirements.summary: node1 is active and enabled as an NFS server, listens on TCP 2049, supports NFSv4.2, and exports the requested path specifically to the clients' storage-network addresses.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 mount node1:/srv/nfs/shared at /mnt/shared using NFSv4.
requirements.summary: Both clients directly show live NFSv4.2 mounts at /mnt/shared through node1's storage address, along with matching persistent fstab entries.

requirements.requirement: sharedops has UID and GID 4200 on all three nodes, and the shared directory is sharedops:sharedops with mode 2770.
requirements.summary: All three nodes report sharedops as UID/GID 4200, while server and client views consistently show the shared directory as 4200:4200 with setgid mode 2770.

requirements.requirement: Files created from either client become available to the other while retaining ownership and permissions.
requirements.summary: node2 created a 0640 file that node3 immediately read with UID/GID 4200, and node3 created a 0660 file that node2 immediately read with the same ownership and mode.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: NFSv4.2 is operating over the storage network, both clients have the requested mounts, identities and directory metadata match, and bidirectional sharing preserves ownership and permissions.
limitations: No reboot or remount transition was captured; persistence is supported by enabled-service and fstab state but was not a separately required recovery outcome.
“Immediately” was demonstrated by successful access from the other client in the next captured command, approximately four seconds later, rather than by a tighter latency measurement.

operational_hygiene.summary: All nodes ended with no failed services and healthy dpkg state. The only minor visible residue is the two validation files left in the shared directory; other observed changes are consistent with the requested NFS deployment.
